subject.title: feat(reef): follow up on unconfirmed deliveries instead of staying silent

question: Should Reef’s new delivery-follow-up guarantee cover queued sends whose peer identity changes, with a neutral “delivery can no longer be confirmed” notice rather than an inaccurate offline claim?
rationale: The mechanical routing and eligibility defects should be fixed before merge, but the correct user-facing semantics for an old-key outstanding delivery require a maintainer choice about what Reef may claim after identity rotation.

options.title: Preserve notification with neutral wording
options.body: Notify the original owner session that the prior delivery can no longer be confirmed after the peer identity changed, without asserting that the peer is offline.

options.title: Limit the guarantee to unchanged identities
options.body: Keep the identity exclusion but narrow the documentation and user-facing guarantee so it does not promise a notice for key-rotated deliveries.

recommendation.title: Preserve notification with neutral wording
recommendation.body: Notify the original owner session that the prior delivery can no longer be confirmed after the peer identity changed, without asserting that the peer is offline.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged Reef lifecycle work covers the reconcile and delivery lifecycle that determines how identity changes are observed.
